key_insight: A physics-informed neural network can train turbulence closures in a solver-agnostic way, making them more generalizable across bluff-body shapes than traditional solver-coupled calibration.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast screening and deployment of stable Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes closures for drag and wake prediction without embedding a CFD solver inside the training loop.
method: Impose the RANS residual directly with automatic differentiation inside a PINN, removing mesh dependence and adjoint derivation.
Train four closure forms across six 2D bluff-body wakes at Re = 10^4, including stress-based and direct-force models.
Improve stability with input-gradient smoothing and a Lipschitz constraint, then test frozen models in a finite-element solver under leave-one-shape-out validation.
evidence_signal: Across in-sample and strict leave-one-shape-out tests, all four closures beat steady SST k-ω, and the force model achieved the best generalization with about 8.5% LOSO drag error.
watch_item: Generalization still depends on training across representative geometries, and solver stability must be verified after the network is frozen and transferred to the CFD solver.
paper_title: Generalizable turbulence closures across bluff-body shapes by PINN-based solver-agnostic training
